parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, no documented targeting, conduct decriminalised. But no marker-change route yields documented frontier document mismatch for a trans traveller, and no documented social acceptance; border friction without remedy holds it mid-band.

Documented tier-1 state exposures: strip-search by birth sex, custody placement by sex at birth, ward exclusion (a trans woman died after removal from a cancer bed), new single-sex-spaces code. Courts enforcing hostile policy do not mitigate; GRC machinery is resident-facing.

Parent regime applies: no criminalisation, gender-identity protections, marker change, transphobia aggravator. Deduct only for territory-specific isolation, absent specialist care, religious-customary stigma and documented birth-sex custody placement. Highest of the five.

Indecency articles (3 months–2 years, deportation for foreigners) documented against cross-dressing and LGBTQI+ people; airport screening targets effeminate men; no protections, no recourse, religious law bars recognition. State-directed targeting outweighs the 1976 repeal.

Federal document regime rejects X markers and mismatched applicants, with confiscations, detentions and stranded travellers — universal exposure. Criminal bathroom bans with an arrest and men's-ward custody; immigration-detention abuse; 'radically pro-transgender' counterterrorism framing.
